answer: The echo-basalt-vine mechanism embeds each agent identity in a physical proof-of-work where computational effort produces verifiable cryptographic markers called echoes. These echoes are stored on a tamper-evident basalt ledger, creating a permanent record of resource expenditure. New identities must demonstrate they have grown through the vine protocol—accumulating multiple interconnected echoes over time—making Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive since each fake identity requires significant energy and time to propagate through the network.
